Random draws inside a graph

Source: R/rng.R
zl_noise_normal.Rd

zl_noise_normal() and zl_noise_uniform() are tensors of draws from the stream named stream, made anew at each training step: at step s of a trainer (1 for the first) element i (in R's order, counting from 0) is position offset + i of the stream at step s. Outside training, zl_forward() uses the trainer's last step, or 0. The values do not depend on the thread count, and equal zl_rng_normal() and zl_rng_uniform() for the same stream, step and positions. Use offset to keep the draws of a split batch the same: a second half of a batch starts at the first half's size.

Usage

zl_noise_normal(dim, stream, offset = 0)

zl_noise_uniform(dim, stream, offset = 0)

Arguments

dim

Dimensions: one to four positive whole numbers.

stream

The stream's name.

offset

The position of the first value.

Value

A tensor.

Details

They have no gradient, and none is needed: nothing flows back into a draw.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
g <- zl_graph(function(x) x$a + zl_noise_normal(c(2, 3), "eps"), p,
              inputs = list(a = c(2, 3)))
zl_forward(g, list(a = matrix(0, 2, 3)))$output
#>            [,1]        [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] -1.0074857 -0.15439574 -0.6295075
#> [2,] -0.2536615  0.09861942  0.7901454
